svg.title: t densities against the standard normal
svg.desc: Three t densities at 2, 5 and 30 degrees of freedom drawn against the standard normal, with a table of the upper 0.975 quantile each one supplies.
svg.text: Replacing sigma by S costs you tail weight, and the cost shrinks with n
Upper 0.975 quantile, the multiplier a two-sided 95 percent interval uses
The multiplier is what the unknown sigma
costs you. At 30 degrees of freedom it runs
about four percent above the normal value;
at 2 degrees of freedom it is more than
